diveTitle: What actually happens when you compress
diveSubtitle: What compression changes in your PDF, and what it leaves alone.
dive1Title: Why do PDFs get so large in the first place?
dive1Desc: Text and vector graphics take up almost no space - the size is almost always driven by embedded images. A PDF exported from a scanner or a phone photo can easily hit tens of megabytes because each page is a full-resolution image, not compressed text.
dive2Title: Lossy vs. lossless - what we actually do
dive2Desc: We use lossy compression on embedded images, re-encoding them at a lower quality and resolution, since that's where nearly all the size reduction comes from. Text and vector content are left untouched - they're already compact and compress losslessly by default.
dive3Title: Compressing scanned PDFs vs. text PDFs
dive3Desc: A scanned PDF, made entirely of images, compresses dramatically - often 70-90% smaller - because there's a lot of image data to optimize. A PDF that's mostly text with a couple of small images has little left to compress, so the reduction will be modest by comparison.
dive4Desc: If a PDF's images were already heavily compressed before being embedded, common with PDFs exported from other online tools, there's not much redundancy left to squeeze out. Re-compressing an already-compressed image mostly just adds generation loss without much size benefit.
dive5Desc: We pick the highest image quality that still fits your target, so a larger target gives a sharper result. With very small targets (20 to 50 KB), photos and scans get noticeably softer, so check a page before you submit or print it.
dive6Desc: You can upload and compress several PDFs in the same batch - each is compressed independently and returned as its own file. Compression ratio varies per file since it depends on each PDF's own image content, not a fixed percentage applied to everything.
faqSubtitle: Quick answers on limits, privacy and results.
faq1Question: How much can I reduce my PDF file size?
faq1Answer: It depends on what's in the PDF. Scanned and photo-heavy files can usually reach 100 KB or 200 KB. Text-only documents are already small and may not go much lower. If your target can't be reached, we tell you and give you the smallest version we could make.
faq2Question: Will the compressed PDF look different?
faq2Answer: Only as much as needed. We use the best quality that still fits the size you chose, so a 500 KB target looks close to the original while 20 KB is visibly softer. Text stays as text and stays sharp.
faq3Question: Can I compress more than one PDF at a time?
faq3Answer: Yes - the free plan lets you compress up to 2 PDFs at once. Starter and Pro allow up to 10 files per batch. We process them all together and give you a zip file to download when there's more than one.
faq4Question: Is there a file size limit?
faq4Answer: On the free plan, each file can be up to 20MB (100MB on Starter). If yours is bigger, try splitting it first with our PDF splitter tool, then compress the parts.
faq5Question: What happens to my files after compression?
faq5Answer: Everything is deleted within one hour of processing. Your files are encrypted during the upload and transfer. We don't read them, keep them, or share them.
seoTitle: When You Need to Shrink a PDF
seoP1: Large PDFs are hard to email and slow to upload. Scanned documents and image-heavy presentations are the usual cause, and the compressor shrinks both with nothing to install.
seoP2: You choose the final size. Pick 20, 50, 100, 200 or 500 KB, or type any size, and we search for the highest image quality that still fits. A 200 KB target usually gives you a file of about 195 to 199 KB, not one far smaller than you needed. If a file can't get that small without becoming unreadable, we tell you.
seoP3: Any PDF works, and scanned documents shrink the most because each page is a full-resolution image. It runs in the browser on desktop, tablet and phone.

guide.title: How to compress a PDF to 100 KB, 200 KB or 1 MB
guide.intro: Upload your PDF above, pick the size your form allows (for example **100 KB** or **200 KB**) and download the result. We land just under that size at the best quality that fits. Scanned and photo-heavy PDFs usually get there easily; PDFs that are mostly text are already small and shrink less.

rows: Photos and scans look softer; text pages stay readable
table.note: Typical results, not guarantees. How small a PDF can go depends on what is inside it.

sections.title: Still too big?
items: Remove the pages you don't need with [Split PDF](/split-pdf), then compress again.
If the PDF is made from phone photos, shrink the photos first with [Compress Image](/compress-image), then rebuild the PDF with [JPG to PDF](/jpg-to-pdf).
If the form accepts more than one file, split a long document into parts and upload them separately.
Working with very large files? The free plan has a size limit per file; paid plans raise it. See [Pricing](/pricing).

sections.title: Will compressing change my text?
sections.text: No. Compression works on the images inside the PDF. Text stays as text, so it remains sharp and searchable.
